_comment: Fill in pipeline IDs and templateParameters here directly, and/or run `@ZedAgent setup-service` — it reads this file first and only prompts for empty/missing entries. templateParameters is a free-form key-value map: the agent passes whatever keys you provide verbatim to ADO. Use {{currentBranch}}, {{excludeStamps}}, {{pubRegions}}, {{ffStamps}}, {{ffRegions}}, {{sdpType}}, {{validateOnly}} as runtime placeholders — the agent substitutes these per release. The _examples block at the bottom shows expected entry shape; delete it once your real entries are in.

canaryRouting._comment: How Steps 5 (canary deploy) and 7 (rollback) pick which pipelines to trigger. mode='static' (default): the agent triggers EVERY entry under canary.* in parallel. mode='cluster-type': the agent runs a Kusto query, parses the DeploymentUnit suffix (e.g., '-sfmc', '-sf'), and uses clusterTypeMap to route each suffix to a canary pipeline key. Use 'static' if your canary pipelines are split by region (one pipeline per region — e.g., DataMover). Use 'cluster-type' if a single canary region hosts multiple cluster-type variants served by separate pipelines (e.g., PROT SFMC/SFRP).

productionRouting._comment: How Step 10 (roll-forward — PROD pipelines targeting canary regions) picks which pipelines to trigger. Same mode semantics as canaryRouting but reads from production.*. Independent from canaryRouting because many services have asymmetric topology (e.g., N canary pipelines + 1 production pipeline).
